findingDetails.title: 5l re-derives the mode-to-packetKind map that 5i already builds in the same call chain
findingDetails.case: A future edit to how packetKind is resolved lands in checkTieBreakOrder but not checkNativeSurfaceLast; 5l then evaluates stale kinds, its surface-only filter misclassifies entries, and the two checks disagree about the same tieBreak.
findingDetails.userImpact: Maintainers must keep two identical derivations in sync; drift shows up as inconsistent 5i/5l verdicts on the same hub-router.json.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both occurrences sit in the one call chain checkHubRouter -> checkTieBreakOrder / checkNativeSurfaceLast (cjs:1339-1340); no third occurrence in the reviewed window (cjs:1140-1369).
findingDetails.recommendation: Hoist a single kindByMode derivation (a small helper, or one map computed in checkHubRouter and passed to both checks) so the packetKind lookup has one home.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Per-check self-containment is the file's prevailing style (checkSubworkflowSignals and aliasDrift build their own structures), which argues against hoisting.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The duplication may be accepted style: every check derives exactly what it needs to stay independently readable.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If maintainers confirm per-check derivation is deliberate policy for this file, this is a note only, not an action item.
